MANILA, Philippines – Senator Bam Aquino recommended making the school-based feeding program the top priority for an additional budget among other Department of Education (DepEd) programs in 2027.
Overall, the Senate finance committee recommended P915.49 billion for the proposed new general appropriations of the DepEd and its attached agencies.
That amount is P4.91 billion higher than the P910.5 billion approved by the House of Representatives, but P1.25 billion lower than the P916.75 billion in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP).
Among the changes, the Senate panel added P11 billion to the school-based feeding program, pushing the proposed allocation to P22.4 billion.

But Aquino, as the DepEd’s budget sponsor, plans to seek an additional increase for the program. “At the proper time, this representation, alongside some other colleagues, will introduce an amendment to increase the budget for the school-based feeding program by P6,265,478,145,” he said during the plenary deliberations.
That would raise the program’s budget to P28.7 billion, higher than the P25.7 billion in the 2026 national budget.

The additional funding would also expand the universal feeding to cover kindergarten to Grade 2, reaching another 1.8 million students in 2027. This follows the phased implementation under the national children’s nutrition bill, which has been ratified but not yet signed into law.
The P28.7-billion budget would cover 124 feeding days, or from June to December in 2027, at P30 per meal.

blocks.text: Aquino remains hopeful that they can still set a higher budget for the education sector.
“I have spoken to the Senate President multiple times to share my frustration with the fiscal space provided for this important agency,” he said in the plenary.

“We have proposed a much bigger budget only to be met with an answer that we didn’t like, which was that the fiscal space is very limited — which we understand. Mr. [Senate] President, I believe that we can still increase this before the period of amendments,” he added in a mix of English and Filipino.
Aquino also supports funding for the Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program in 2027. There is no separate line item for it in the 2027 NEP.
However, in the Senate committee report, the ARAL Program remains unfunded.
“Talo pa tayo ng House. P300 million, nakalagay sila. Tayo, wala,” Senator Joel Villanueva said during his interpellation. (The House outdid us. They allocated P300 million. We did not put anything.)
Villanueva noted that 11 million students have been identified as needing remediation sessions in school year 2026-2027.
Aquino told senators that the ARAL Program still has unspent funds from this year. During the 2026 budget talks, it was the Senate that pushed P8.9 billion for the learning recovery initiative.

“More than half of the P8.9-billion budget for this year was released very late, only in July and August. Therefore, because of the late release, meron pa pong pondo, ‘yon ang gagamitin (there is still funding, which will be used) next year,” he explained.
He added that the disbursement rate, which refers to actual payments made, is only at 13%.

According to Aquino, the DepEd is already in the process of disbursing the funds in the next few weeks, with Education Secretary Sonny Angara promising a faster process. Angara was standing beside the senator during the deliberations.
“We know that it can work. We’ve been talking about our learning gaps for so many months. The main solution to the learning gap is really a remediation program,” Aquino said. – Rappler.com
